statement: >= 15 distinct organisations have a training run >= 1e26 FLOP (Epoch AI, snapshot 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Count at end-2024 = 0 on public estimates. The largest known runs were ~4-5e25 FLOP (Gemini 1.0 Ultra ~5e25; Llama 3.1-405B 3.8e25, largest open-weight). A Bloc A regulator's draft reporting rule (Sept 2024) said its 1e26 threshold 'exceeds all or virtually all models in use' and that 0-15 domestic firms exceeded its model or cluster thresholds. 100k-GPU clusters able to run 1e26-scale training came online in H2 2024 but no such run was public by year-end. Compute tracker trend: 4-5x/year growth; 2e29 FLOP feasible by 2030.

items.summary: Compute tracker: training compute of notable and frontier models grew 4-5x per year (2010-May 2024); the largest known runs were ~2e25 and ~5e25 FLOP, i.e. no run yet at 1e26. Organisation count 0.
items.detail: Epoch AI, Sevilla & Roldán, 'Training compute of frontier AI models grows by 4-5x per year', 2024-05-28 (verified via search snippet): GPT-4 2e25, Gemini Ultra 5e25 FLOP.

items.summary: A Bloc A platform company released the largest open-weight model to date, trained with ~3.8e25 FLOP (about 2.6x below 1e26).
items.detail: Meta Llama 3.1-405B, released 2024-07-23; 'The Llama 3 Herd of Models' reports 3.8e25 FLOP on up to 16k H100s. Value well known; paper not re-extracted this run. arXiv v1 dated 2024-07-31.

items.summary: Compute tracker analysis: on power, chip, data and latency constraints, training runs of ~2e29 FLOP will likely be feasible by 2030; the largest runs to date were of order 5e25 FLOP. Implies many 1e26+ runs within a few years if the trend continues, though not how many organisations.
items.detail: Epoch AI, 'Can AI scaling continue through 2030?', August 2024 (verified via search; Epoch thread dated ~2024-08-20).

items.summary: A Bloc A developer announced a 100,000-GPU training cluster brought online in ~4 months, with plans to double it; such a cluster can in principle run a 1e26 FLOP training within a few months.
items.detail: xAI 'Colossus' (Memphis, 100k H100), announced by Elon Musk on X ~2024-09-02/03. Verified via web_extract against the NVIDIA press release 'NVIDIA Ethernet Networking Accelerates World's Largest AI Supercomputer, Built by xAI' (2024-10-28): 100,000 Hopper GPUs, built in 122 days, being doubled to 200,000; feasibility note is our arithmetic (1e5 x ~1e15 FLOP/s x 40% x 30 days ~ 1e26).

items.summary: A Bloc A regulator proposed quarterly reporting for training runs above 1e26 operations and clusters above 1e20 OP/s; it assessed that 0-15 domestic companies exceeded its model or cluster thresholds and that the 1e26 threshold 'exceeds all or virtually all models in use'.
items.detail: Bloc A BIS proposed rule 'Establishment of Reporting Requirements for the Development of Advanced AI Models and Computing Clusters', 89 FR (2024-09-11; announced 2024-09-09), verified via Federal Register snippet. Implements EO 14110 s.4.2.

items.summary: No public compute estimate at or above 1e26 FLOP existed by end-2024, but several late-2024 flagships had undisclosed compute, so the count of 0 is a floor based on public estimates.
items.detail: E.g. OpenAI o1 (2024-12-05), Gemini 2.0 (2024-12-11) had no disclosed compute. Epoch's later database entries are not used here (strict as-of).
